Equilic Quad

GeometryTrianglesCircles
Game: This is a picture, not a game: three equal-sided triangles sit on a four-sided shape, and their three top tips always land on one straight line.
How to play: Drag S around the circle, or C and D along the sloping lines. You can also focus a point and use the arrow keys; tick the boxes to show names, angle marks or a hint.
Look for the math

The old page still shows the Java applet (with a "browser is not set to run Java applets" fallback). Its statement is due to Jack Garfunkel: build equilateral triangles on AC, DC and DB, away from AB, and their tips P, Q and R line up. Drag the three handles and watch the red line: it never bends.

The four-sided shape

A, B and S lie on one circle. C is placed on the line from B to S and D on the line from A to S at the same distance from B and A, so AD = BC. The two lines meet at S at 60°, which is what makes ABCD an equilic quadrilateral. In this picture AD and BC are marked with matching ticks when you tick "Angle marks".

Turn each side by sixty degrees

The page's proof uses a rotation of 60° about A: triangle AQB is equilateral, so it carries B to Q, and triangle ACP is equilateral, so it carries C to P. Therefore the segment BC lands on PQ: those two lengths are equal and differ in direction by 60°. A second 60° turn about B carries AD onto QR, so AD = QR too.

One straight line

Because AD = BC, the two lengths PQ and QR are equal. The turns point them along the same straight line, so P, Q and R are one line; S, where AD and BC meet, lies on that line as well. The logic test checks this, the three equilateral triangles and the length equations on thousands of dragged positions, and finds no exception.

What the test also found

The proof's middle step needs S on the arc of the circle away from the chord AB, which is where the starting picture puts it. If you drag S onto the arc between A and B, the triangles still have collinear tips, but triangle AQB is no longer equilateral and the triangles are no longer "away from AB": the drawing keeps the same turn, while the page's wording describes only the starting arc. The applet itself allows both arcs; the test records both rather than hiding the difference.

Try "Hint" to see the two sides of triangle AQB that carry B to Q, then drag S around the whole circle.
